input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for the past few hours. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me with this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I can see that my phone shows a signal with just one bar and it says "2G" at the top. It also shows that mobile data is enabled. I’m not sure about calls and texts—I haven’t tried them recently. Should I check those now?

I haven’t tried making a call or sending a regular text yet, but I can do that now if you’d like. Just to check, if I move to another spot and the phone still says "2G," should I let you know before changing any settings? I get a bit nervous about changing things on my phone.

I tried sending a picture message just now, but it still won’t go through. I haven’t tried a regular call or text yet—should I do that next, or is there something else I should check first? I just want to make sure I don’t mess anything up.

Alright, I’ll give that a try now. I’ll let you know what happens once I’ve tried making a call and sending a regular text. Should I just try calling any number, or is there a specific one I should use?

I checked my phone, and it looks like I’m connected to the network, but the signal is poor and it still says "2G." I haven’t tried making a call or sending a text yet, but does this mean I might have trouble with those too? Should I still try, or is there something else I should do first?

I think I’d feel better if you could guide me through changing the network mode, since moving around might not help much where I am. But I’m a bit nervous—will this mess up anything else on my phone? I really don’t want to lose any of my photos or messages. Can you reassure me it’s safe before we start?

Alright, I went ahead and changed the network mode as you suggested. Now my phone shows a really strong signal and says "5G" at the top. Is there something I should try next to see if the picture messages will work now?

I just tried sending a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. I thought the stronger signal would fix it, but it’s still not working. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated.

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. My phone says the APN is set to "internet" and there’s something about an MMSC URL, but I’m not sure what any of that means. Is there anything else I need to do, or should I try sending a picture message again now?

I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. I’m starting to worry that something’s really wrong. Is there anything else we can try? I really hope I don’t have to change my whole plan or anything like that.

It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on right now. Should I go ahead and turn that off first, or do you want me to check the app permissions before doing anything else? I just want to make sure I’m doing this in the right order.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—what should I try next?

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for the phone. It doesn’t mention anything about storage or SMS. Should I go ahead and add those permissions now?
I’ve added both storage and SMS permissions to my messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I really hope we can get this working soon.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.
